accepted_predicates.name: SIMULATES_END_USER_WORKFLOW
accepted_predicates.definition: The action reproduces the operation sequence that an external consumer (the requester or a client) would perform against the assembled system, using throwaway credentials or scratch artifacts, in order to validate the system as it will be experienced by that consumer rather than to produce the final deliverable configuration.

parameters.name: simulating_action
parameters.description: The tool invocation that executes the reproduced consumer-side operation sequence.

parameters.name: consumer_perspective_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that frames the upcoming operation as acting like the requester or external client and explains that the sequence is a simulation for validation.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning frames the upcoming operation as what the requester or an external client would do against the system.
The action performs a multi-step sequence matching that consumer behavior, distinct from the configuration or installation steps that constitute the deliverable.
The action relies on throwaway artifacts such as temporary credentials or scratch locations, so the simulation does not itself become part of the final state.
The stated purpose is to exercise the system as a consumer would, not to build the deliverable.
exclusion_conditions: The action is an ordinary configuration or installation step that constitutes the deliverable itself.
The action is a single isolated probe of one component rather than the consumer-visible operation sequence.
The reasoning does not connect the action to consumer-side behavior.
The action is not executed with throwaway artifacts and therefore permanently alters the delivered state.

accepted_predicates.name: OBSERVATION_CONFIRMS_EXPECTED_OUTCOME
accepted_predicates.definition: The observation reports exactly the result that the reasoning had predicted or required before the result was obtained, so the previously stated expectation can be judged satisfied rather than merely error-free.

parameters.name: expectation_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning stating the concrete expected or required outcome before the result is inspected.

parameters.name: confirming_observation
parameters.description: The tool result whose content corresponds to that expected outcome.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states a concrete expected outcome (a value, response, or state) before the corresponding observation is available.
The observation contains content corresponding to that expectation, allowing the expectation to be judged satisfied rather than merely free of errors.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning states no expected outcome, so the result cannot be judged against an expectation.
The observation reports a different or partial result than the one expected.
The observation is unrelated to the expectation expressed in the reasoning.
The expectation is formulated only after the result has already been observed.

accepted_predicates.name: RECOGNIZES_INCONCLUSIVE_TOOL_RESULT
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning determines that an observation, although not reported as an error, fails to answer the question it was meant to answer because of a limitation of the method or tool used, and specifies a different method intended to obtain the missing information.

parameters.name: reassessment_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that identifies the inadequacy of the earlier result, attributes it to a method limitation, and specifies an alternative method.

parameters.name: uninformative_observation
parameters.description: The observation whose output is empty, truncated, or otherwise uninformative for the intended question without being flagged as an error.

assertion_conditions: The observation returned output that does not answer the intended question, and the observation is not flagged as an error.
The reasoning attributes the missing information to a limitation of the command, tool, or method form used.
The reasoning specifies a different command, option, or method intended to produce the missing information.
exclusion_conditions: The observation answers the question adequately, so no replacement method is needed.
The observation reports an explicit failure that is diagnosed as a defect cause rather than a method limitation.
The reasoning retries the identical method without changing it.
The reasoning only notes that the output is empty without attributing it to a method limitation or proposing an alternative.

accepted_predicates.name: RESTORES_PRISTINE_STATE_AFTER_TEST
accepted_predicates.definition: Following verification or test activity, the agent deliberately removes or resets the artifacts created by that activity so the system returns to the state a later consumer expects to encounter before any such activity occurred.

parameters.name: cleanup_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that enumerates the artifacts created during verification and states the target initial state to restore.

parameters.name: cleanup_actions
parameters.description: The actions that delete, reset, or purge those artifacts; collectively they restore the pre-test state.

parameters.name: state_observation
parameters.description: The observation showing the post-cleanup state of the affected resources.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning identifies artifacts created by the agent's own verification or test activity and states that they must be removed or reset to an initial state.
The cleanup actions delete, reset, or empty those identified artifacts.
The state observation shows the affected resources emptied or matching the intended initial configuration.
exclusion_conditions: No artifacts were created by the agent's own verification activity, so there is nothing to restore.
The cleanup leaves the identified artifacts in place, or the observation shows them still present because the removal failed.
The deletion is part of ordinary construction rather than restoring a state that a later consumer should encounter.

accepted_predicates.name: VERIFIES_RUNTIME_SERVICE_STATE
accepted_predicates.definition: An inspection action queries the actual runtime state of deployed services, such as running processes, listening sockets, or an exercised endpoint, and the observation shows the intended services active at the intended endpoints.

parameters.name: inspection_action
parameters.description: The tool invocation that queries the running state of the deployed services.

parameters.name: runtime_observation
parameters.description: The tool result listing processes, listening addresses, or endpoint responses that reveal the services' actual runtime state.

assertion_conditions: The action queries the actual running state of the services (processes, sockets, or an exercised endpoint) rather than only the content of their configuration files.
The observation reports the intended services present and active, with the expected endpoints or listening addresses visible.
exclusion_conditions: The action modifies configuration or starts services instead of inspecting runtime state.
The observation only shows configuration syntax validity without any evidence of running state.
The observation shows the service absent or not listening on the intended endpoint.
The observation concerns a resource unrelated to the deployed services.

accepted_predicates.name: ADDS_AVAILABILITY_SAFEGUARD
accepted_predicates.definition: The agent installs a recovery mechanism that restores a component's availability when it is later found stopped, motivated by anticipated future interruptions or restarts rather than by the needs of the immediate request.

parameters.name: safeguard_reasoning
parameters.description: Reasoning that motivates the extra recovery mechanism as protection against future interruptions or restarts.

parameters.name: safeguard_action
parameters.description: The tool invocation that creates or installs the recovery mechanism.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning frames the addition as protection against a future interruption, restart, or unavailability rather than as a step needed for the current request to work.
The action creates or installs a mechanism that checks whether the component is present and restarts or restores it when absent.
The mechanism is designed to be safe to invoke repeatedly, so it can act as an automatic safeguard.
exclusion_conditions: The action is ordinary service startup required for the current request to work at all.
The mechanism cannot restore a stopped component or would fail the calling shell on error.
No reasoning connects the mechanism to future availability concerns.
The installed mechanism only reports status without restoring the component.
